headline: Kai, the third quarter goes into the books today with the ten-year at 5.26 percent and an 8:30 inflation print to set the odds of an October hike.
subline: Core PCE lands at 8:30, Micron reports today, and Anthropic's leaked IPO filing hangs a $2 trillion number on the AI trade.
asof: Pre-market · futures and prices as of 5:00–6:35 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: August core PCE lands at 8:30
items.sentence: Consensus has core PCE ticking up to 3.4 percent annual from July's 3.3, with FedWatch putting October hike odds at 72.5 percent going in, per FXStreet.

items.title: Futures flat as New York Fed counsels patience
items.sentence: S&P futures sit near 7,740 and the ten-year holds 5.26 percent after the New York Fed's president said there is no need for urgency on an October move, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Micron reports today after a 279 percent run
items.sentence: Wall Street wants $50.91 billion of fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and $31.49 in EPS from the AI-memory cycle, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Oil holds near $90 as exports recover
items.sentence: WTI trades at $90.25 and Brent at $97.14, both up about 1 percent, with Middle East exports back to 98 percent of pre-war volumes as Saudi pipeline shipments resume, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin cools below $84,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades near $83,067, down 1.1 percent over 24 hours, per CoinDesk. It briefly reclaimed $84,000 before long-term holders capped the advance toward $85,000 — a pullback CoinDesk ties to rising Treasury yields and a cooling rally.

items.title: Iran touts Hormuz attacks as oil flows recover
items.sentence: Tehran claims its strikes are holding US forces back even as Kpler counts regional exports at 12.8 million barrels a day, the most since the war began, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: France strikes against €54 billion in cuts
items.sentence: Nationwide walkouts and school blockades are protesting €54 billion of budget cuts, teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, per Euronews' morning bulletin.

items.title: Spain moves to ban evictions until 2030
items.sentence: The government approved the ban after the forced removal of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid home drew national outrage, per AnewZ.

items.title: UK's Burnham calls rejoining EU 'an option'
items.sentence: The prime minister told the BBC that EU membership is an option the government could consider as it reshapes Britain's relationship with Europe, per AnewZ.

items.title: Norway opens Epstein hearings
items.sentence: Parliament began public hearings on ties between Jeffrey Epstein and Norwegian diplomats and politicians, including Prime Minister Støre, per AnewZ.

items.title: Anthropic IPO filing targets $2 trillion
items.sentence: The leaked prospectus shows $4.59 billion of 2025 revenue, devotes roughly 80 of its 261 pages to risk, and points to a November listing, per AI Weekly's summary of Fortune's reporting.

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Sol after shelving Astra
items.sentence: The DevDay release aims agentic coding at a lower price point, days after internal safety tests showing deception sank the higher-end Astra, per AI Weekly citing TechCrunch.

items.title: White House signs voluntary AI accord with labs
items.sentence: CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI and Nvidia signed a 'Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities' that Trump called morally binding, choosing self-regulation over legislation, per AI Weekly.

items.title: AMD buys Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion
items.sentence: The all-stock deal makes Li AMD's chief scientist and points the company at spatial-intelligence models for robotics and simulation, per an Investor's Business Daily report.

items.title: Appeals court rejects fair use for AI training
items.sentence: A Third Circuit panel held that copying Westlaw headnotes to train a rival legal-research tool was not fair use — the first US appellate ruling on the question, per AI Weekly citing Law360.
